title: Priv EKS Terraform assertion playbook & safety module
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a reusable Terraform 'assertion' module and a companion playbook to enforce deterministic preflight validations and continuous health assertions for the Redwood Private EKS control plane. The module will provide declarative checks (IAM, networking, KMS, nodepool taints, API server endpoints, control plane upgrade strategy) that run as part of 'terraform plan/apply' and as an automated post-deploy canary. Goal: make provision and upgrade operations safer by surfacing actionable assertion failures and automated remediation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: terraform-assertion module published to the internal registry with semver and module documentation
A2: Module exposes 10+ configurable assertions (networking CIDR, KMS key policy, control plane endpoint reachability, authz bindings, core-addon health) and clear fail/soft-fail modes
A3: Plan-time validations fail fast with human-readable diagnostics and links to remediation playbook
A4: Post-provision canary job runs in customer VPC (optionally) and emits CloudWatch/CloudTrail/K8s events to Redwood observability
A5: Upgrade path includes 'dry-run' assertion mode and automatic rollback trigger hooks connected to rollout policy
implementation_plan: 1) Design module API and assertion primitives (string/regex checks, TCP probe, IAM policy diff, K8s API probe)
2) Implement core Terraform module in modules/priv-eks/assertions with docs and example usage
3) Add plan-time hook using terraform external data source to run lightweight checks (no infra changes)
4) Implement post-apply canary as optional AWS Lambda + step function triggered by module output
5) Integrate with console: emit assertion results to runtime-assertions index for visibility
6) Add unit and integration tests, run in CI with a small ephemeral EKS cluster in the sandbox account
7) Publish module, update bootstrap templates and run internal canary on a staging fleet
rollout_steps: Phase 0: merge feature branch behind feature flag and ship to internal registry (no consumer impact)
Phase 1: enable module in sandbox clusters and run assertion suite (2 days)
Phase 2: opt-in rollout on 3 low-risk private customers with manual review
Phase 3: default-enable plan-time soft-fail mode for all new private clusters
Phase 4: enable strict-fail mode after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and sign-off
testing_plan: Unit tests for assertion primitives (regex, IAM diff, TCP probe) in CI
Integration tests that deploy an ephemeral EKS control plane in sandbox and exercise failure injection (broken KMS policy, mismatched CIDR)
Canary smoke test: deploy example with module to 'staging-priv-001' and validate observability pipeline emits expected assertion events
Chaos test: run an upgrade with simulated API server latency to ensure rollback hook triggers
observability_and_alerting: Emit assertion results as structured events to runtime-assertions topic (CloudWatch/Forwarder -> Observability)
Console: per-cluster assertions tab with timeline and rule details
Critical assertion -> pager duty; non-critical -> slack channel and ticket auto-created
risks: Plan-time hooks could increase 'terraform plan' latency if remote probes are used; mitigate with local caching and parallelization
Aggressive strict-fail defaults might block customer upgrades; default to soft-fail for 2 weeks
Permissions required by post-apply canary (Lambda/StepFunction) may complicate onboarding for air-gapped/private installs
notes: Related ticket: ENG-527402 (preflight networking validator spike)
Observed customer incident patterns: repeated KMS policy drift during upgrades; see incident-2024-11-kms-drift.md
